newsitem.title: USA: Tosco hydrocracker up in 8 to 10 wks - union.
newsitem.headline: Tosco hydrocracker up in 8 to 10 wks - union.

text.p: A hydrocracker damaged in last week's fire at the Tosco refinery in Martinez, Calif., could return to service in eight to 10 weeks, said an official for the union representing the refinery's workers.
"The preliminary guess is that it will be back in eight to 10 weeks," said Jeff Dodge, president of the Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers (O.C.A.W) Union, local chapter 1 - 5.
The 32,000 barrel-per-day unit, which turns fuel oils into gasoline, exploded and caught fire January 21 after a hydrocarbon line ruptured, Dodge said.
One worker was killed and 25 injured in the blaze, which has reduced capacity at the 156,000 bpd refinery east of San Francisco.
Plant officials were not immediately available for comment on the return date or affects of the fire on operations.

Dodge said refinery and state officials will appear before Contra Costa County Board of Supervisors in a regularly scheduled meeting Tuesday. The Tosco refinery and several other are located in the county.
The board passed an ordinance in December putting local refineries and other industrial sites under tighter scrutiny when they shut for overhauls or maintenance.
Local refiners filed two lawsuits against the county this month, alleging there were procedural and due process errors when the board passed the ordinance, board members said.
